notes.wakayima: The clever trickster of Ganda folktales.
notes.kintu: The first man in the Ganda creation story.
notes.nnambi: Kintu’s wife, daughter of Ggulu (the sky).
notes.walumbe: Nnambi’s brother: death, in the legend.

guidebook.intro: Ganda folktales (**enfumo**) are told in the evening. The two most famous are the tricks of **Wakayima** the hare, and the legend of **Kintu**, the first man.

tips.title: Wakayima the trickster
body: The small hare beats bigger animals by cleverness: he tricks the elephant, the lion and the leopard. The lesson is usually **obugezi businga amaanyi** (wisdom beats strength), though sometimes Wakayima is caught out by his own lies.

tips.title: Kintu and Nnambi
body: **Kintu** lived alone with his cow until **Nnambi**, daughter of **Ggulu** (the sky), married him. Ggulu told them to leave quickly before her brother **Walumbe** (Death) could follow.
On the way, Nnambi went back for the millet she had forgotten for her chicken. **Walumbe** followed her, and that is why death came to the earth.

culture.title: Retelling
body: A good storyteller opens with **Olwatuuka olwali olumu**, gets the listeners to answer, and ends with the lesson: **Enfumo eno etuyigiriza nti…**. Now you can tell one too. Congratulations on reaching the last unit!
